questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the front-end and back-end of a compiler.

S1: The front-end includes phases that are independent of the target hardware.
S2: The back-end includes phases that are specific to the target hardware.
S3: The back-end includes phases that are specific to the programming language used in the source code.

Identify the CORRECT option.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Front end (lexical, syntax, semantic analysis, intermediate code) depends on the source language, not on the target machine [latex]\text{---}[/latex] S1 TRUE.
- Back end (code optimization for the machine, code generation) is specific to the target hardware [latex]\text{---}[/latex] S2 TRUE.
- The back end works on intermediate code, so it is independent of the source language [latex]\text{---}[/latex] S3 FALSE.

Answer: Only S1 and S2 are TRUE

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Only S1 and S2 are TRUE.
S1, S2, and S3 are all TRUE.
Only S1 and S3 are TRUE.

questions.text:
Which one of the following sequences when stored in an array at locations
A[1], . . . , A[10] forms a max-heap?
questions.solution:
Max-heap: every parent [latex]A[i]\ge[/latex] its children [latex]A[2i][/latex], [latex]A[2i+1][/latex].

- Option 1: A[3] = 10 has child A[6] = 14 False
- Option 2: 23 [latex]\ge[/latex] 17, 14; 17 [latex]\ge[/latex] 7, 13; 14 [latex]\ge[/latex] 10, 1; 7 [latex]\ge[/latex] 5, 6; 13 [latex]\ge[/latex] 12 True
- Option 3: A[5] = 13 has child A[10] = 15 False
- Option 4: A[4] = 1 has children 12, 7 False

Answer: 23, 17, 14, 7, 13, 10, 1, 5, 6, 12

questions.text:
Let SLLdel be a function that deletes a node in a singly-linked list given a pointer to the node and a pointer to the head of the list. Similarly, let DLLdel be another function that deletes a node in a doubly-linked list given a pointer to the node and a pointer to the head of the list.
Let n denote the number of nodes in each of the linked lists. Which one of the following choices is TRUE about the worst-case time complexity of SLLdel and DLLdel?
questions.solution:
To delete a node we must update its predecessor's next pointer.

- Singly linked list: the predecessor is found only by walking from the head [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(n)[/latex].
- Doubly linked list: the node's prev pointer gives the predecessor directly [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(1)[/latex].

Answer: SLLdel is O(n) and DLLdel is O(1)

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: SLLdel is O(1) and DLLdel is O(n)
Both SLLdel and DLLdel are O(log(n))
Both SLLdel and DLLdel are O(1)
SLLdel is O(n) and DLLdel is O(1)

questions.text:
Consider the Deterministic Finite-state Automaton (DFA) [latex]A[/latex] shown below. The DFA runs on the alphabet {0, 1}, and has the set of states {s, p, q, r}, with s being the start state and p being the only final state.

Which one of the following regular expressions correctly describes the language accepted by [latex]A[/latex]?
questions.solution:
From s: 0 goes to dead state r, so a string must start with 1 (reaching final state p).
At p: 0 loops on p; 1 goes to q, and from q only another 1 returns to p (0 goes to r).

So after the first 1, we repeat "0" or "11": [latex]1(0+11)^*[/latex].

Answer: [latex]1(0+11)^*[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
The Lucas sequence [latex] L_n [/latex] is defined by the recurrence relation:
[latex] L_n=L_{n-1}+L_{n-2}, \; for \; n\geq 3, [/latex]
with [latex] L_1=1 \; and \; L_2=3 [/latex]
Which one of the options given is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Let [latex]\varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}[/latex] and [latex]\psi=\frac{1-\sqrt5}{2}[/latex]. They satisfy [latex]x^2=x+1[/latex], [latex]\varphi+\psi=1[/latex], [latex]\varphi\psi=-1[/latex].

Check [latex]L_n=\varphi^n+\psi^n[/latex]:
- [latex]L_1=\varphi+\psi=1[/latex] True
- [latex]L_2=(\varphi+\psi)^2-2\varphi\psi=1+2=3[/latex] True
- It satisfies [latex]L_n=L_{n-1}+L_{n-2}[/latex] because both [latex]\varphi,\psi[/latex] satisfy [latex]x^2=x+1[/latex].

Answer: [latex]L_n=\left(\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}\right)^n+\left(\frac{1-\sqrt5}{2}\right)^n[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
